title: Speeding up planning decisions with AI
gist: DeepMind says its Gemini-based PlanAssist cut officer time on householder planning assessments by 58% in pilots at three English councils, with over 70% of reports approved unedited. It is moving to a 12-month Beta with 15 councils, aiming for all English councils in 2027.

insights.claim: In early pilots across Barnet, Camden and Dorset councils, PlanAssist cut average planning officer time on householder assessment tasks by 58%.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Quantified productivity gain from generative AI in a public-sector workflow.
insights.quote: bring the average time a planning officer spent on householder assessment tasks down by 58%

insights.claim: More than 70% of reports PlanAssist generated were approved by officers with no edits required.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: High first-pass acceptance suggests output quality is usable, not just fast.
insights.quote: more than 70% of the reports generated by the tool

insights.claim: Pilots have run since June 2026 and the results are described as encouraging but early.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Evidence base is short and limited to three councils.

insights.claim: Routine householder applications make up up to 70% of planning officers' workloads, are often simple to approve, yet consume a disproportionate share of time.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Large, repetitive, automatable workload share explains why the use case fits AI.

insights.claim: Planning bottlenecks slow progress toward the UK government's goal of 1.5 million new homes by 2029 and leave families waiting months for simple works like loft conversions.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Links AI tooling to housing supply and growth policy.

insights.claim: PlanAssist validates documents and drawings, checks heritage constraints and local and national policies, checks prior objections, and drafts fully cited reports that officers can edit.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Shows an end-to-end agentic workflow with citations rather than a chat tool.

insights.claim: The design keeps a qualified planning officer reviewing and approving every assessment before any decision, positioning AI as support rather than decision-maker.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Human-in-the-loop framing eases regulatory and political acceptance of public-sector AI.
insights.quote: planning officers retain the final say on every application

insights.claim: PlanAssist is built with Gemini and developed by Google DeepMind with the UK government, Google Cloud and Faculty.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Gemini gets a flagship government deployment reference.

insights.claim: PlanAssist enters a 12-month Beta on live applications, onboarding 12 more councils in three cohorts to reach 15 in total, mixing metropolitan and rural districts.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Defines the rollout timeline and test diversity.

insights.claim: Subject to successful testing, the government plans to make the tool available to all councils in England in 2027.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Possible nationwide public-sector deployment is a template for other AI-in-government sales.

insights.claim: The tool is part of a broader Google DeepMind partnership with the UK government to explore AI transforming planning and other public services.
insights.speaker: Owen Larter and David Thacker
insights.so_what: Signals further public-service AI deals are likely.
